theme.title: Full-Court Mix
theme.subtitle: Teams, stars and stories from across basketball
theme.recap: The best numbers come from all over basketball history. Which answer surprised you most?

questions.prompt: Other Eastern Conference finalists are charted. How many regular-season games did Dwight Howard's 2008–09 Magic win?
questions.note: 59–23, then Orlando upset LeBron's top-seeded Cavaliers in the East finals.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the team finished the regular season with a 59–23 record

funFacts.text: Dwight Howard became the youngest Defensive Player of the Year winner that spring.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: becoming the youngest player to win the award

funFacts.text: A shoulder injury to All-Star Jameer Nelson forced Orlando to reshape its backcourt.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Jameer Nelson left a game after dislocating his right shoulder

funFacts.text: Hedo Türkoğlu hit a game-winner against Philadelphia in the opening playoff round.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Hedo Türkoğlu's game winner in game four of that series

questions.prompt: Kawhi Leonard was 22 when he won Finals MVP in 2014. How old was rookie Magic Johnson when he won it in 1980?
questions.note: Just 20. With Kareem injured, the rookie point guard started the clinching Game 6 at center.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: one who had left college after only two years, and was only 20 years old

funFacts.text: Johnson started Game 6 at center and ended up playing all five positions.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: started the game at center and eventually played all five positions in a dominating performance

funFacts.text: He had left Michigan State after only two college seasons.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: one who had left college after only two years, and was only 20 years old

funFacts.text: Kawhi Leonard's 2014 award made him only the third-youngest Finals MVP.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Leonard was the third-youngest recipient of the award (22 years and 351 days old)

questions.prompt: In Luka's historic 60-point triple-double against the Knicks, how many rebounds did he pull down?
questions.note: 21, alongside 60 points and 10 assists: the first 60-point, 20-rebound triple-double in NBA history.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: points (60) and rebounds (21)

funFacts.text: Dallas escaped with an overtime victory over the Knicks after a remarkable rally.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: 126–121 victory over the New York Knicks

funFacts.text: This was the first 60-point, 20-rebound triple-double in league history.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: first player in NBA history to record a 60-point, 20-rebound triple-double

funFacts.text: Luka also eclipsed Dirk Nowitzki's old Mavericks single-game scoring record.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: previously held by Nowitzki (53)

questions.prompt: Stephen Curry's record overtime in 2016 was 17 points. How many did Tracy McGrady score in the final 35 seconds to stun San Antonio in 2004?
questions.note: 13: four straight threes, one of them a four-point play and the last a game-winner in the final two seconds.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: scoring 13 points in the final 35 seconds against the San Antonio Spurs

funFacts.text: Houston acquired McGrady from Orlando in a seven-player deal that also sent Steve Francis and Cuttino Mobley away.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: McGrady, Juwan Howard, Tyronn Lue, and Reece Gaines were traded to the Houston Rockets as part of a seven-player deal

funFacts.text: The burst was four straight threes, one a four-point play and the last a game-winner in the final two seconds.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: one of which was part of a four-point play and the last of which was a game-winner in the final two seconds

funFacts.text: That Rockets team rebounded from a losing start and finished the season fifth in the West.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: After the All-Star break, Houston rebounded from their slow start, finishing the season with 51 wins

questions.prompt: How far, in feet, was Damian Lillard's famous 2019 playoff series-winning buzzer-beater over Paul George?
questions.note: 37 feet. Dame waved goodbye to OKC after burying a deep series winner.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Damian Lillard scored 50 points in Game 5 and finished off the series by hitting a 37-foot three at the buzzer to break a 115–115 tie

funFacts.text: Dame had a huge scoring game even before that shot.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Damian Lillard scored 50 points in Game 5

funFacts.text: It was not his first series-winning shot from deep.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: his first came against Houston in 2014

funFacts.text: The game ended the Westbrook–George partnership in OKC.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: This was also the last Thunder game to feature both Russell Westbrook and Paul George
